stem.en: A country votes every year, but only candidates chosen by the ruler may contest, and critics of the ruler are punished. Is voting alone enough to make it democratic?

text.en: Yes, because the people vote every year, and voting makes a country democratic.
Yes, because a large turnout proves the people support the ruler.
No, because people have no real choice and cannot express their opinions freely.
No, because a real democracy has only one strong party.

explanation.en: Voting alone is not enough. A democracy also needs a real choice of candidates, freedom to express opinions and criticise the government, and limits on the power of the people who win. A large turnout does not prove free support where critics are punished, and a democracy does not need one strong party: many parties can compete.

hints.en: Besides voting, what else must people be free to do?
